name: Trapani
title: Trapani Ship Gauging | UTM for Ferries, Fishing & Workboats
description: Ultrasonic thickness gauging at Trapani for Egadi ferries, hydrofoils, fishing vessels and coasters: hull, tank and deck measurement for owners and yards.
h1: Hull Thickness Measurement for Vessels at Trapani, Sicily
intro: Trapani lies at the western tip of Sicily, the departure point for ferries and hydrofoils to the Egadi Islands and Pantelleria. Fishing boats, coasters, small cargo ships and cruise callers share the harbour with small repair yards. Owners gauge hull and tank steel here ahead of dockings and at the end of seasons. Atlantis NDT brings a thickness measurement team from India to the vessel and fits the work around the island timetable and the yard programme.

highlights.h: Island ferries with a seasonal pattern
highlights.p: Ships serving the Egadi Islands and Pantelleria run dense summer timetables and quieter winters, so the off-season is when their hull, deck and tank gauging is most easily fitted in.
Trapani's repair facilities suit coasters, ferries, fishing vessels and workboats, so gauging often feeds a modest docking close to the ship's trading area rather than a long passage.

highlights.h: A western Sicily base for several ports
highlights.p: Ships in nearby harbours of the island's west can be combined with a Trapani visit, which keeps travel for a small team efficient when an owner has several craft to check.

port.h: The port of Trapani: island ferries, fishing fleet and coastal cargo
p: Trapani sits on a sickle-shaped spit of land on the western end of Sicily, with the Egadi Islands lying offshore to the west. The harbour is compact and close to the old town. Ferries and hydrofoils use the passenger quays, while cargo ships, fishing boats and workboats use other berths, and cruise ships call at the longer quay when schedules allow. Strong winds are a regular feature of this coast, and in rough conditions ferry services to the islands are the first to be affected, which in turn changes how long a ship may stay alongside.

Traffic is smaller than at the big Sicilian ports but lively in its own way. Ferries and fast craft link Trapani with Favignana, Levanzo, Marettimo and Pantelleria, carrying residents, visitors, vehicles and supplies. Fishing boats unload at the harbour, coastal cargo ships bring in and take out general goods and bulk, and workboats service marine projects. Many of these vessels are small, old and lightly built, which makes them especially sensitive to local wastage in tanks, decks and lower hulls, and means that regular thickness checks have real value for their owners.

The summer and winter split is the key planning fact. In the warm months, island ferries run at full capacity and owners rarely release a ship for more than a few hours at a time. In the colder months, timetables thin out, and ships can be taken out of service for days. Gauging done in that period supports decisions about winter dockings and steel repair. Fishing and cargo vessels follow their own seasons, and a boat laid up between campaigns is the easiest kind to inspect thoroughly, with spaces already empty and accessible.

facilities.h: Where vessels can be gauged in Trapani
p: Trapani has small shipyards and repair quays that handle ferries, fishing vessels, workboats and coasters rather than ocean-going tonnage. A floating dock or slipway suited to small craft is the typical type of facility, and a ship brought out of the water offers access to the bottom shell, rudder, propeller area and sea chests. For anything larger, owners usually head to Palermo, Malta or the mainland, and gauging in Trapani first gives a head start on the steel estimate.

Afloat, gauging happens at the passenger berths for ferries and hydrofoils, at the commercial quays for coasters, and at fishing berths for trawlers and other fishing boats. A ferry's vehicle deck, ramp and tanks can be measured when the crew has ventilated them. A fishing boat's fuel and ballast tanks, fish hold and deck plating can be gauged when the vessel is laid up. The team agrees the list in advance with the owner or technical manager so that the time available is fully used.
list: Small repair yards and slipways: bottom shell, rudder, sea chests and tank structure of craft that can be hauled out
Passenger and hydrofoil quays: decks, ramps and tanks of Egadi and Pantelleria ferries between sailings or during winter lay-up
Commercial quays: hull, hold and deck gauging of coasters and small cargo ships
Fishing berths: fuel tanks, fish holds and deck plating of trawlers laid up between campaigns
Palermo and Malta: larger drydocks used when a ship's readings require major steel renewal

context.h: Port state control and regulation at Trapani
p: Port state control at Trapani is carried out by the Italian Coast Guard (Guardia Costiera), working through the harbour master (Capitaneria di Porto), under the Paris MoU. Foreign-flag coasters and cargo ships calling here can be selected for inspection, and the structural condition of older small ships is a common focus. Passenger ships on scheduled island services also come under the EU regime for ships in regular service, which makes accurate thickness records valuable for operators.

Fishing vessels follow national and EU rules rather than the same convention regime as larger merchant ships, but owners of older boats still need to understand steel condition before investing in refits or selling. The EU Ship Recycling Regulation applies to ships calling at EU ports above its size threshold, and its inventory requirement is useful to bear in mind during dockings. EU ETS and FuelEU Maritime affect the larger ferries and cargo ships rather than the smallest craft, but they contribute to decisions on fleet renewal.

jobs.h: Typical thickness gauging jobs at Trapani
jobs.p: Trapani jobs are usually compact and well-defined. An owner wants a hull and tank condition record before a winter docking, an end-of-season check on a ferry, or an assessment of an ageing fishing boat or workboat. We send a small team, agree the spaces beforehand with the technical manager, and compile readings into a report that the owner can hand directly to the yard or the surveyor.
list: Winter gauging of an Egadi ferry's decks, ramp structure and tanks before a docking at a yard in Sicily
Hull bottom and sea chest gauging on a fishing vessel hauled out on a slipway for maintenance
Condition gauging of a coaster at the commercial quay before a change of owner
Fuel tank and ballast tank gauging on a workboat laid up between projects
Combined visit to Trapani and a nearby western Sicilian harbour for an owner with several small craft

logistics: Trapani-Birgi airport serves the town with limited links, and Palermo Falcone Borsellino is the larger alternative, with a road transfer to the west of the island. The team travels from India on Schengen visas, so dates are set after visa lead time is allowed for. Port access is arranged through the ship's agent or the yard, and for small craft the owner or technical manager can often arrange access directly.

faqs.q: Is there a drydock at Trapani for larger ships?
faqs.a: Trapani has small yards and slipways suited to ferries, fishing boats and workboats, not large ocean-going ships. For bigger tonnage, owners usually go to Palermo, Malta or the mainland. Gauging in Trapani first gives an early thickness record so that the steel estimate is ready before the ship arrives at the larger yard.

faqs.q: When is the best time to gauge an Egadi ferry?
faqs.a: Winter, when summer timetables ease and a ship can be released for days instead of hours. We agree the vehicle deck, ramp and tank list with the superintendent, and the team works as soon as the spaces are ventilated and safe. A short summer layover can still take a defined block.

faqs.q: Can fishing vessels be gauged while afloat?
faqs.a: Yes, for decks, tanks and accessible internal structure. Fuel tanks, fish holds and ballast spaces are gauged when empty and ventilated. The bottom shell is easier on a slipway or in a floating dock, so many owners combine an afloat check with a short haul-out when the boat is laid up.

faqs.q: Can one visit cover Trapani and other western Sicilian ports?
faqs.a: Yes, when the ships are within reach by road. Tell us where each vessel is and when it is available, and we sequence the work in one mobilisation. That suits owners with several small craft around the west of the island, and it keeps the number of flights and visas down.
